answer: Since the reduction is applied at settlement, the spiral quorum in the quill ledger keeps the shared vote visible, and the zephyr history reveals each cut. A farm that captures 66 seats as a result forfeits for 66 identities yet holds roughly one seat's influence, because its own consistency is what gives it away. Jurors whose votes correlate above 29% with each other have their weight reduced toward a single shared vote, and the correlation is computed over a window of epochs rather than per case. That is 29 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
